result:
Rain taps against the windowpane, a rhythmic drumming that slows the pulse of the house to a crawl. The streets outside vanish, swallowed by a curtain of water. There's a peculiar comfort in these suspended hours, when gray light bleeds into every corner, turning the room into something softer, dreamlike. A cup of tea beside me cools slowly, steam curling up to join dust motes dancing in the dim light. The glass is cool under my fingertips, a tactile anchor to the moment. I watch a droplet trace a path down the pane, merging with others until the world smears into an impressionist painting. Time feels different here, less linear, more circular. It curls around the arms of the reading chair like a cat.

Thoughts drift like debris in a slow river, uncollected and free. Old memories surface and sink without judgment. A childhood summer, a forgotten melody, the face of a friend seen only in passing. They float by, leaving no ripple. The rain asks only for attention. It whispers that stillness is not emptiness, but a vessel waiting to be filled with the resonance of being alive. I listen to the hum of the refrigerator, the growl of a passing car, the scratch of my breath. The rhythm of the drops syncs with my heartbeat; the house creaks, settling into its bones, sharing the silence.

Eventually, the rain will cease and life return. For now, the gray embrace holds everything safe. The sky promises to break, colors to sharpen, voices to rise. Yet I hold this breath suspended in the gray, savoring the art of waiting.
